data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A halted run is resumable without corrupting append-only identity iff the event log's identity structure (hash chain or equivalent) is self-verifying up to its last persisted entry AND the resumption procedure appends new events by linking to the last verified entry, treating the log as the sole source of truth and ignoring any non-persisted runtime state. Resumption must be refused iff the self-verification fails OR if the system cannot continue from the verified log alone\u2014i.e., it requires runtime state (model internals, open file handles, environment) that is not encoded in or reconstructable from the event log. The key insight: resumption safety is not about how the halt happened but about whether the log is a sufficient and intact continuation point.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Self-verification of the log fails: the hash chain is broken at some point, so there is no valid last entry to link from.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log verifies but the system's next-event generation depends on process-internal state (e.g., attention cache, intermediate activations) not encoded in the event log and not reconstructable by replay.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log verifies but events in it reference external resources (tool-call responses, fetched data) that are no longer available, so replay to reconstruct state fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log verifies but the budget state was stored separately and is inconsistent with the event log, so the resumed run's resource-gated decisions diverge.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reframe the question around the log's self-sufficiency rather than the halt's circumstances. The event log carries append-only identity via a digest chain; if that chain verifies, the log is structurally sound regardless of why the run stopped. The resumption question then reduces to: can the system generate the next event using only the verified log as input? If yes, append the next event linking to the last verified entry\u2014identity is preserved because the chain is extended correctly. If no\u2014because the system needs state that only existed in the halted process's memory or external environment and cannot be reconstructed\u2014resumption would produce events that are not a faithful continuation, so refuse. This framing subsumes the clean-halt condition (a torn write fails self-verification) and the non-determinism condition (unreconstructable state means the log is not sufficient).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
